records.title: Position size from fixed dollar risk
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Entry $25.00, stop $24.50: distance $0.50; $100 risk / $0.50 = 200 shares.

records.title: Position-size rounding down
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $75 / $0.40 = 187.5 shares; round down to 187, producing $74.80 planned price risk.

records.title: Gap risk beyond a stop
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 100 shares entered $20 with $19.50 stop imply $50 planned risk; a hypothetical $19.10 fill implies $90 price loss.

records.title: Portfolio heat sum
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Three planned risks of $60, $80, and $40 sum to $180 portfolio heat.

records.title: Risk as percent of equity
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $120 planned risk / $24,000 equity = 0.005 = 0.5%.

records.title: Planned reward-to-risk ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Entry $40, stop $39.20 gives $0.80 risk; target $41.60 gives $1.60 reward; ratio=2.0.

records.title: Breakeven win rate before costs
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Average win $150 and loss $100: $100/($150+$100)=40%.

records.title: Arithmetic expectancy per trade
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 45% wins×$120 minus 55% losses×$70 = $54−$38.50=$15.50.

records.title: Maximum drawdown from equity peaks
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Equity peaks at $10,500 then troughs at $9,450: decline $1,050, or 10%.

records.title: Recovery percentage after a loss
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $10,000 falls 20% to $8,000; recovering $2,000 requires $2,000/$8,000=25%.

records.title: Limit-order price boundary
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A $15.00 buy limit may fill at $14.98 or $15.00, not above $15.00 under ordinary handling.

records.title: Market-order execution uncertainty
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A fictional buy consumes 100 shares at $10.00 and 50 at $10.08: average=(1000+504)/150=$10.0267.

records.title: Bid-ask spread cost
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Bid $30.00, ask $30.10, midpoint $30.05; a buy at ask is $0.05 above midpoint, or $5 on 100 shares.

records.title: Slippage in basis points
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Expected buy $50.00, fill $50.10: $0.10/$50×10,000=20 bps adverse.

records.title: Partial fill and remaining quantity
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Order 500 shares; executions 120 and 180 total 300; remaining quantity is 200.

records.title: Stop-limit trigger and limit
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Sell stop $19.50, limit $19.40; a jump from $19.60 to $19.20 triggers but is below the acceptable sell limit.

records.title: Trailing-stop reference path
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A $1 trail from a high of $25 gives $24 stop reference; new high $26.20 raises it to $25.20.

records.title: Order-cancellation race
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A 200-share order receives a 50-share fill, then cancel is requested; a later 30-share fill leaves 120 only after cancel confirmation.

records.title: Time-in-force boundary
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A day limit remains eligible during its broker-defined session and expires unfilled with 0 of 100 shares executed.

records.title: Current ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Current assets $9 million / current liabilities $6 million = 1.50.

records.title: Quick ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Cash $3m + receivables $4m divided by $5m current liabilities = 1.40.

records.title: Working capital
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $12m current assets − $9m current liabilities = $3m working capital.

records.title: Gross margin
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Revenue $20m − cost $12m = $8m gross profit; $8m/$20m=40%.

records.title: Operating margin
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Operating income $2.4m / revenue $16m = 15%.

records.title: Net margin
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Net income $1.2m / revenue $24m = 5%.

records.title: Revenue growth rate
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Revenue rises from $40m to $46m: ($6m/$40m)×100=15%.

records.title: Basic versus diluted EPS
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $10m earnings / 5m basic shares=$2.00; /6m diluted shares=$1.67.

records.title: Simplified free cash flow
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Operating cash flow $7m − capital expenditures $2m = $5m.

records.title: Simple cash runway
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Cash $12m / quarterly burn $3m = 4 quarters.

records.title: Debt-to-equity ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Debt $18m / equity $12m = 1.50.

records.title: Interest coverage
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: EBIT $6m / interest $2m = 3.0 times.

records.title: Inventory turnover
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: COGS $24m / average inventory $6m = 4.0 turns.

records.title: Receivable days
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Average receivables $5m / annual sales $50m ×365 = 36.5 days.

records.title: Book value per share
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Common equity $45m / 15m shares = $3.00 per share.

records.title: Price-to-earnings ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Price $30 / trailing EPS $2 = 15×.

records.title: Price-to-sales ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Market cap $120m / annual revenue $60m = 2.0×.

records.title: Simplified enterprise value
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Market cap $100m + debt $30m − cash $20m = $110m.

records.title: Enterprise value to sales
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: EV $150m / annual revenue $75m = 2.0×.

records.title: Share-count dilution rate
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Shares rise from 20m to 25m: (5m/20m)×100=25%.

records.title: Arithmetic mean return
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Returns 2%, −1%, and 3% sum to 4%; 4%/3 = 1.33%.

records.title: Geometric mean return
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Returns +10% then −10% give factors 1.10×0.90=0.99; two-period geometric mean is sqrt(0.99)−1≈−0.50%.

records.title: Log return
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Price $50 to $52 gives ln(52/50)=ln(1.04)≈3.922%.

records.title: Sample variance
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Values 2,4,6 have mean 4; squared deviations 4+0+4=8; sample variance=8/(3−1)=4.

records.title: Standard deviation of returns
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: If sample variance is 0.0004, standard deviation=sqrt(0.0004)=0.02=2%.

records.title: Downside deviation
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Target 0%; returns 2%, −3%, −1% have shortfalls 0, −3%, −1%; squared sum=0.001; declared divisor 3 gives sqrt(0.001/3)=1.826%.

records.title: Return covariance
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Paired deviations A: +2%,−2%; B:+1%,−1%; products 0.0002 and 0.0002; population covariance=0.0002.

records.title: Correlation coefficient
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Covariance 0.00015, standard deviations 0.02 and 0.01: correlation=0.00015/0.0002=0.75.

records.title: Beta from covariance
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Covariance 0.0003 / market variance 0.0002 = beta 1.5.

records.title: Simple regression alpha
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Mean asset return 1.2%, beta 1.1, mean market return 0.8%: alpha=1.2%−1.1×0.8%=0.32%.

records.title: Simple Sharpe ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Mean return 1.0%, risk-free 0.2%, deviation 2.0%: (1.0−0.2)/2.0=0.40.

records.title: Simple Sortino ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Mean 0.9%, target 0.1%, downside deviation 1.6%: 0.8/1.6=0.50.

records.title: Simple Calmar ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Annual return 12% / 20% maximum drawdown = 0.60.

records.title: Historical-quantile value at risk
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Twenty fictional daily returns sorted worst to best; the chosen 5% convention selects the single worst, −4%, so reported loss threshold is 4%.

records.title: Simple expected shortfall
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Worst three returns are −6%, −4%, −2%; their average is −4%.

records.title: Tracking error
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Active returns 1%, −1%, 0%; mean 0%; sample deviation=sqrt((0.0001+0.0001)/(3−1))=1%.

records.title: Information ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Average active return 0.4% / tracking error 1.0% = 0.40.

records.title: Upside capture ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Across selected up periods portfolio totals 12% and benchmark totals 10%; simple ratio=120%.

records.title: Downside capture ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Portfolio totals −6%, benchmark −10%; magnitude ratio=60%, indicating smaller sampled decline.

records.title: Portfolio weight from market value
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Holding $12,000 in a $60,000 portfolio has weight $12,000/$60,000=20%.

records.title: Weighted portfolio return
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Weights 60% and 40%, returns 5% and −2%: 0.6×5%+0.4×−2%=2.2%.

records.title: Rebalance trade amount
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $100,000 portfolio, 30% target=$30,000; current holding $24,000 requires $6,000 purchase before costs.

records.title: Equal-weight allocation
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $24,000 across 6 holdings gives $4,000 each, or 16.67% before rounding.

records.title: Simple volatility risk contribution
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Weight 30% × volatility 20% gives 6 percentage-point weighted volatility exposure.

records.title: Cash weight
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $8,000 cash / $40,000 portfolio = 20%.

records.title: Simple portfolio turnover
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Purchases $30,000, sales $25,000, average assets $100,000: turnover=25%.

records.title: Indicated dividend yield
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Quarterly dividend $0.25 implies $1 annualized; $1/$20=5%.

records.title: Simple payout ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Dividends $4m / net income $10m = 40%.

records.title: Ex-dividend reference adjustment
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Prior close $30 and $0.40 dividend gives mechanical reference $29.60.

records.title: Split-adjusted share count
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 200 shares at $50 under 2-for-1 become 400 at $25 reference; both equal $10,000.

records.title: Rights offering subscription ratio
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: One new share per 5 rights; holder of 500 rights can subscribe for 100 shares.

records.title: Warrant intrinsic value
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Stock $12, strike $10, one warrant per share: intrinsic value=max($2,0)=$2.

records.title: Convertible conversion shares
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $1,000 principal / $20 conversion price = 50 shares.

records.title: Equity option contract notional
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 2 contracts ×100 shares×$30 = $6,000 underlying notional.

records.title: Call intrinsic value
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Underlying $55, strike $50: max($5,0)=$5 per share, or $500 for multiplier 100.

records.title: Put intrinsic value
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Strike $40, underlying $36: max($4,0)=$4 per share, or $400 for multiplier 100.

records.title: Option breakeven at expiration
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Strike $50 plus $3 premium gives $53 expiration breakeven.

records.title: Option premium total cost
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Premium $1.25 ×100×3 contracts=$375 before fees.

records.title: Entry price versus quoted price
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 60 shares fill at $10.04 and 40 at $10.10; average entry=(60×10.04+40×10.10)/100=$10.064.

records.title: Cumulative partial-fill reconciliation
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A 500-share order fills 180 shares; 500−180=320 shares remain only if the order is still open.

records.title: Limit-order price protection
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A buy limit of $24.50 while the ask is $24.70 remains unfilled; the limit protects price but supplies no fill.

records.title: Stop trigger versus fill price
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A sell stop triggers at $15.00 after a gap and fills at $14.72; 100 shares realize $28 more loss than a $15.00 assumption.

records.title: Position size from risk budget
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $120 risk budget and $0.75 planned risk per share give floor(120/0.75)=160 shares before costs.
records.sourceResearchScope: CME describes risk-based size from planned stop distance and account risk; 160 shares is an independent whole-share fictional case.

records.title: Portfolio heat from open planned risk
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Open risks of $90, $140, and $70 total $300; against $20,000 equity, planned heat is 1.5%.
records.sourceResearchScope: Risk per position is stop distance × size; open portfolio heat is the sum of non-negative planned stop losses divided by equity.

records.title: Scale-in weighted average cost
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 100 shares at $12 and 50 at $13 produce ($1,200+$650)/150=$12.3333 average before fees.

records.title: Scale-out realized and open quantity
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: From 300 shares at $10, selling 120 at $10.80 realizes $96 before costs and leaves 180 shares open.

records.title: Break-even with round-trip costs
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 200 shares entered at $25 with $8 declared round-trip costs require $25.04 per share to break even before omitted costs.

records.title: R-multiple realized outcome
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Initial risk $150 and realized net profit $225 produce +1.5R.
records.sourceResearchScope: The Van Tharp Institute explicitly defines R-multiple as realized gain/loss divided by initial planned risk; original 225/150=1.5R arithmetic.

records.title: Maximum adverse excursion
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Long entry $30; lowest eligible trade before exit is $29.25, so price MAE is $0.75 or 2.5% of entry.

records.title: Maximum favorable excursion
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Long entry $12.50; highest eligible trade is $13.40, so price MFE is $0.90 or 7.2%.

records.title: Time stop and elapsed market minutes
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Entry 10:05, rule 30 wall minutes, evaluation 10:35: the time condition is met, but exit still requires an executable order.

records.title: Trailing reference without lookahead
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Completed lows are $20.10, $20.25, $20.40; a rule using the lowest of those references $20.10 before the next bar.

records.title: Gap risk and position loss
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 150-share long enters $22 with planned exit $21.50 but fills after a gap at $20.90; gross loss=(22−20.90)×150=$165.

records.title: Halt exposure in an open position
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 200 shares remain long when trading halts after a $9.60 last trade; no reopen quote is supplied, so current executable value is unknown.

records.title: Short-position borrow cost
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $5,000 borrowed-value basis at 18% annualized for 3/360 year estimates $7.50 borrow cost.
records.sourceResearchScope: SEC explains borrowed shares and financing costs; Nasdaq describes stock lending fees and borrow availability.

records.title: Short-squeeze risk is not a signal
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Reported short interest 4 million and dated float estimate 20 million imply 20%, but no future covering demand is known.
records.sourceResearchScope: FINRA distinguishes reported short positions from daily short-sale volume; short interest/dated float alone does not establish future covering demand.

records.title: Correlated positions and shared risk
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Three equal long positions all lose 4% when a shared sector shock occurs; three tickers did not create three independent outcomes.

records.title: Daily loss-limit state
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Realized −$180, declared included fees −$20, and limit −$200 place the account exactly at its limit.
records.sourceResearchScope: CME trade-plan self-evaluation explicitly includes a daily total-dollar loss limit; fictional realized loss plus fees reaches the declared threshold.

records.title: Risk-of-ruin model limits
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Equal +1R/−1R outcomes yield +0.10R expectancy at 55% wins but −0.04R at 48%.
records.sourceResearchScope: Risk-of-ruin models require explicit thresholds, risk size, payoff distribution, horizon and dependence assumptions; original +1R/-1R examples measure expectancy only.

records.title: Expectancy from an outcome distribution
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 40% at +2R, 50% at −1R, and 10% at 0R gives 0.4×2−0.5=+0.3R.

records.title: Win rate and sample size
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: 18 wins among 30 eligible completed cases produce 60%; three open cases are excluded.

records.title: Profit factor denominator
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Gross profits $900 and gross losses −$600 produce profit factor 900/600=1.5.

records.title: Maximum drawdown from an equity path
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Equity peaks at $12,000 then reaches $10,800; drawdown is $1,200 or 10% of that peak.

records.title: Return with external cash flow
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Account starts $10,000, receives $2,000 immediately, and ends $12,600; simple return on $12,000 invested is 5%.
records.sourceResearchScope: CFA Institute distinguishes time-weighted from money-weighted returns when external cash flows affect a portfolio; the fictional immediate-deposit shortcut is defined explicitly.

records.title: Arithmetic versus geometric return
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: +50% then −50% has arithmetic mean 0%, but $100 becomes $75 and geometric return is about −13.4% per period.

records.title: Volatility annualization assumption
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Daily volatility 1.2% annualized with √252 is about 19.0% under the stated convention.
records.sourceResearchScope: CFA Institute notes that daily volatility × sqrt(number of business days) assumes uncorrelated daily returns; 1.2%×sqrt(252)≈19.0% is a conditional illustration.

records.title: Survivorship bias in a sample
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Ten stocks start; two delist after large losses. Measuring only eight survivors excludes 20% of the starting names.
records.sourceResearchScope: QuantConnect's explicit survivorship-bias section describes the danger of excluding delisted historical constituents; fictional 2/10 omission=20%.

records.title: Lookahead bias and filing availability
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Quarter ends March 31, filing appears May 8; an April 15 screen cannot use the filed value.

records.title: Revenue growth with comparable periods
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Comparable quarterly revenue rises from $40m to $46m; growth=(46−40)/40=15%.

records.title: Gross margin and consistent units
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Revenue $80m and cost of revenue $52m give gross profit $28m and margin 35%.

records.title: Operating cash flow versus net income
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Net income is $12m and operating cash flow $7m; the $5m difference requires reconciliation, not automatic fraud inference.

records.title: Current ratio and classification
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Current assets $30m and current liabilities $20m give a current ratio of 1.5.

records.title: Diluted EPS and share count
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: $10m available income divided by 5m diluted weighted-average shares gives $2.00 diluted EPS.

records.title: Stock split and per-share comparability
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Before a 3-for-1 split, 100 shares at $60 become 300 shares near $20; position value remains $6,000 before market movement.

records.title: Cash dividend and ex-date interpretation
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Price moves from $40 to $39.60 across a $0.50 dividend; raw price return is −1%, while pretax simple total return is +0.25%.

records.title: Rights offering and dilution context
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: One new share per four old shares could add 2.5m shares to 10m outstanding if fully exercised, a 25% increase.
records.sourceResearchScope: SEC-hosted issuer materials provide concrete rights-offering ratios and dilution disclosures; fictional 1-for-4 on 10m shares adds 2.5m if fully exercised.

records.title: Reverse-split mechanics
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: A 1-for-10 reverse split turns 1,000 shares near $0.80 into 100 shares near $8, preserving $800 before movement.

records.title: Filing amendment and version control
records.fictionalWorkedCase: FICTIONAL: Original filing May 1 reports 12 units; amendment May 10 reports 10. A May 5 decision must retain 12 as then-known.
